blocks.x: IoT, Twin & Robotics applied to Last-Mile & Urban Logistics. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Last mile is the costliest mile: route density, delivery promise, failed-delivery economics and urban access rules. Dynamic routing, fleet telemetry and micro-hub orchestration decide whether the final mile makes money.

Governance inherits the sector frame — Urban access/LEZ rules among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Logistics & Supply Chain level this capability reads as: gate, yard and dock telemetry into appointment systems (dwell time down 25-40%). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
